searchText: So I'm digging into forkchoice changes. Your change to `get_ancestor()` is a bit complex. There's a trivial simpler version that's closer to the existing spec, but it would return something slightly different. If we have blocks: (`B1`,`B2`,`B3`) with roots: (`R1`,`R2`,`R3`) and slots: (`S1`, `S2`, `S3`) Then your existing `get_ancestor()` function when called with `get_ancestor(Store, R3, S1)` would return `ChildNode(R1, S1, is_parent_node_full(B2))` while the trivially modified version of this function would return: `ChildNode(R1, S1, is_payload_present(Store, R1))` In other words, your existing `get_ancestor(Store, R3, S1)` function will return whether the chain from `B1` to `B3` is built with the payload for `B1` as present. The trivial version of this function will return whether the PTC voted that it is present The trivial version would be this: ```python def get_ancestor(store: Store, root: Root, slot: Slot) -> ChildNode: block = store.blocks[root] If block.slot > slot: return get_ancestor(store, block.parent_root, slot) return ChildNode(root=root, slot=slot, is_payload_present=is_payload_present(store, root)) ``` I'm not sure I understand the significance of the difference. I assume this difference is what motivated the more complex version of this function Yeah you can't use the PTC vote because the actual attestation chain may be different than the PTC vote. That is, the PTC may not vote for a Payload to be timely but the next proposer for example build on it anyway And attestations that voted for full will be miss counted if you use PTC

So I'm digging into forkchoice changes. Your change to `get_ancestor()` is a bit complex. There's a trivial simpler version that's closer to the existing spec, but it would return something slightly different.

If we have blocks:
(`B1`,`B2`,`B3`)
with roots:
(`R1`,`R2`,`R3`)
and slots:
(`S1`, `S2`, `S3`)

Then your existing `get_ancestor()` function when called with `get_ancestor(Store, R3, S1)` would return
`ChildNode(R1, S1, is_parent_node_full(B2))`
while the trivially modified version of this function would return:
`ChildNode(R1, S1, is_payload_present(Store, R1))`

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: In other words, your existing `get_ancestor(Store, R3, S1)` function will return whether the chain from `B1` to `B3` is built with the payload for `B1` as present. The trivial version of this function will return whether the PTC voted that it is present

excerpts.content: Yeah you can't use the PTC vote because the actual attestation chain may be different than the PTC vote. That is, the PTC may not vote for a Payload to be timely but the next proposer for example build on it anyway
